meta.title: ShortPulse — Local AI Short-Form Video Agent
meta.description: Turn a topic or script into a ready-to-post vertical video. Script, voiceover, captions, visuals and music, assembled on your own machine — no subscription.

topic.title: Give it a topic

features.title: Everything short-form video needs, none of it gated

local.title: Runs on your machine
local.detail: Self-host it and scripting, voiceover, transcription, visuals and rendering all execute locally — only stock footage touches the network. The hosted service trades that away deliberately: it has no GPU, so the script and the AI stills come from paid APIs.

captions.title: Word-synced captions
captions.detail: faster-whisper gives word-level timing, so captions highlight one word at a time instead of dumping a full line.

languages.title: 9 languages
languages.detail: Script, voiceover and subtitles generate natively in English, Turkish, Spanish, German, Arabic and more.

music.title: Auto-ducked music
music.detail: Background music sidechain-ducks under the voiceover automatically — no manual mixing.

stills.title: Photoreal stills or real footage
stills.detail: A RealVisXL still per scene with a Ken Burns move over it, or a matching Pexels clip. Self-hosting with a GPU adds local text-to-video, which this service doesn't run.

outro.title: Branded outro card
outro.detail: An optional closing card rendered locally with Pillow, so the last frame is your call-to-action, not a diffusion guess.

comparison.title: What changes when it's local and open

limits.title: Built to survive scrutiny
limits.intro: Marketing pages hide the rough edges. Ours are in the README, in full — here are a few of them, so you know before you clone it:
limits.stills: AI stills draw faces convincingly and extremities badly — hands, feet and full-body shots are where a frame falls apart, so the script engine keeps people in close and medium shots. Legible text is beyond the model entirely: it cannot write a label, a sign or a book cover.
limits.aiVideo: ai_video (local text-to-video) only runs where you supply the GPU. It is not available on this hosted service: renting one costs more per video than the mode is priced at, so we would rather not offer it than offer it badly.
limits.llm: Small local LLMs occasionally under-count scenes; the script engine retries and drops malformed ones rather than failing the render.
limits.stock: Stock footage is a closest-match, not a guarantee — Pexels clips can be loosely related to the scene.

output.a: A 1080x1920 MP4, H.264/AAC, with the voiceover, word-synced captions burned in, background music ducked under the voice, and an optional closing card. No watermark, on every plan including the free credits.

duration.q: How long does a render take?
duration.a: On this service, a short with stock footage takes about 45 seconds end to end. AI stills take one to two minutes: the images come from a hosted GPU at roughly 8 seconds each, but the first one after a quiet spell waits for the model to load. Self-hosted on an Apple Silicon M-series the stills are much slower — about 78 seconds per scene, so ~7 minutes for a short — because your own machine is doing the diffusion.

languages.a: Nine: English, Turkish, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Arabic, Russian and Italian. Script, voiceover and subtitles are all produced in the language you pick. Japanese is missing because Piper ships no Japanese voice we can use commercially.

script.q: Can I use my own script?
script.a: Yes. Paste it and the LLM only splits it into scenes and writes the visual prompts — your wording reaches the voiceover untouched.

posting.q: Do you post to TikTok or YouTube for me?
posting.a: No. ShortPulse renders the file and hands it to you; publishing is still your job. If auto-posting is the feature you actually want, another tool will serve you better today.

ownership.q: Do I own what I make?
ownership.a: Yes. Download it and do what you like with it. When you use the stock-footage mode, credit the videographers in your post description — the project page collects the names and links for you, and Pexels' licence requires it.

pricing.a: Credits, bought once. A render costs 1 credit with stock footage and 3 with AI stills, doubled for medium length and tripled for long. You see the exact cost before you start it. (Local text-to-video is 10, and only applies if you self-host — it is not offered here.)

expiry.a: No. Nothing renews and nothing resets monthly — the ledger has no expiry, so credits sit there until you spend them.

failure.a: The credits go back automatically. Refunds are tied to the project and can only happen once, so a failure can't leave you charged for a video you never got.

freeTier.q: Is there really a free tier?
freeTier.a: {credits} credits when you sign up, no card. One of your videos can use AI stills — that one is on us, so you see the paid mode before deciding anything — and the rest of the grant renders stock-footage videos at 1 credit each. Re-rolling a scene and further AI-stills renders need a credit pack.

diy.q: Can I run this myself instead?
diy.a: Yes, and it costs nothing. The whole thing is MIT — clone it, point it at your own Ollama and GPU, and there are no accounts, no credits and no limits. Credits exist only because the hosted instance runs on hardware somebody pays for.

local.a: When you self-host, yes: scripting, voiceover, transcription, image generation and rendering all run on your machine, and the one stage that reaches the network is stock footage from Pexels. This hosted service is the trade-off — it has no GPU, so scripts come from OpenAI and AI stills from Replicate. Voiceover, captions and rendering still happen on our server, and the code is the same either way.

roughEdges.a: AI stills draw faces well and extremities badly — hands, feet and full-body shots are where a frame falls apart — and legible text is beyond the model entirely. Local text-to-video needs a serious GPU, which is why this service doesn't offer it at all. Small local LLMs sometimes return fewer scenes than asked. All of it is in the README's Known limitations section.

artStyles.title: Six looks, one prompt away
artStyles.sub: Every frame below is a real render — same model, same settings, same subject. We picked a subject with a face and hands on purpose, because that's the hardest thing to get right and the reason most of these looks are stylized.

captionStyles.title: The part that actually holds attention
captionStyles.sub: Captions are timed per word by faster-whisper, so the active word highlights on the syllable it's spoken. Pick how that looks — size, colour, placement and how many words sit on screen at once.

editor.title: Every scene, lined up against the video
editor.sub: When a render finishes you get the whole breakdown next to the player — what the voice says, how long each scene runs, and where it sits in the timeline.

generate.title: What's this <accent>video</accent> about?
generate.intro: Give it a topic — everything below already has a sensible default, so you can hit generate now and come back to fine-tune later.

upload.title: A video you <accent>already have</accent>.
upload.intro: Upload it and every spoken word gets timed and burned in — the same captions the generator produces, on your own footage. Or pick another language and it is spoken again over your picture.
upload.dropHint: MP4, MOV, WebM or MKV · up to 200MB · needs an audio track
upload.pickAnother: Click to pick a different file
upload.spokenLanguageHint: Telling it the language up front stops short clips getting mis-detected.
upload.clipsOnHint: The transcript is read for the moments that stand up on their own. Each one is cut out and lands in your library as its own video, captioned and ready to edit. Videos from 2 to 60 minutes.
upload.clipsOffHint: Leave this alone to caption the whole video as it is.
upload.dubWithClipsHint: Take the clips first, then dub the ones you keep.
upload.dubOnHint: The speech is translated and spoken again over your original picture. Nothing about the video changes, so if you are on camera your lips won't match the new language — dubbed video normally looks like this.
upload.dubOffHint: Leave this alone to keep the original audio and only burn in captions.
upload.focusPlaceholder: e.g. the part where he explains the pricing
upload.focusHint: Optional. The transcript still decides — if nothing in it matches, you get no clips and your credits back.
upload.windowHint: Drag to pick the stretch to read. Only this part is transcribed, and it is what you pay for — 1 credit per {perCredit} minutes. At least {minutes} minutes.
upload.templateHint: Sets the caption style, where it sits and the frame. Change any of them below afterwards.
upload.templateNeedsClips: Captioning keeps the frame it was filmed in — pick a look with a different frame when you cut it into clips.
